description: Provenance ledger of the decode docs (01-06, 13): one row per quantitative claim with the value as measured at the current units, the research-workspace experiment ID or bundled file that holds it, and the scope it was measured on. status 'supported' means the docs' figure equals the value in the row.

claims.claim: 0x235 / 0x237 ACC frames start 0.2 s after the first CAN frame (median 0.23 s)
claims.value: median 0.23 s, range 0.15-0.46 s on 26 of 27 cold starts (one at 0.83 s)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-462; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: 27 cold starts of the owner's research captures; the one late start is at 0.83 s.

claims.claim: 0x191 target summaries start with the ACC frames, 0.2 s after the first CAN frame
claims.value: starts together with 0x235 (same frame time within 10 ms): median 0.23 s, 0.15-0.46 s on 26/27, max 0.87 s
claims.note: Same frame time as 0x235 within 10 ms on every cold start of the owner's research captures.

claims.claim: openpilot's fingerprinting is done and it starts transmitting at 3.3-4.2 s after the first CAN frame (14 cold starts, current openpilot)
claims.value: first sendcan: newer drives (0x78+, 14 cold starts) 3.3-4.15 s (one 0.9 s); older drives (0x02-0x10, 13) 6.7-8.1 s (two ~1.0-1.2 s); overall median 4.04 s
claims.note: Older openpilot builds (13 cold starts, 0x02-0x10) start transmitting at 6.7-8.1 s, after the 0x80 object records begin at 5.83-6.12 s; the start time follows the software version.

claims.claim: 0x680 frames start with the ACC frames at 0.2 s; the first tracked object appears at a median 0.8 s (0.65-1.3 s on 24 of 27 cold starts)
claims.value: 0x680 frames at 0.15-0.46 s (median 0.23 s, with the ACC frames); first non-idle object (range > 1 code or lateral != 0) median 0.78 s, 0.65-1.29 s on 24 of 27 cold starts; the other 3 report it at 2.7, 4.2 and 11.7 s
claims.source: research workspace SCR-462; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Non-idle object = range above 1 code or a nonzero lateral code.

claims.claim: A newborn track read about 39 m for a car about 100 m ahead and reached 105 m within 5 s of its birth
claims.value: drive A seg A18 track 26: init template at 46.22 s, plateau 34-42 m (median 38.9 m) until 48.65 s, then 45->105 m in 2.6 s, 107.0 m at 51.36 s (age 86), peaks 109 m; 4.9 s from birth to 105 m
claims.note: Drive A, segment A18, track 26; the car distance of about 100 m is read from the camera image in the figure (docs/img/shots/young_track_convergence.jpg).

claims.claim: Survival of the age-5 decision by ego speed and object speed (44 / 65 / 60 / 85 % at ego speed up to 2 m/s; 7 / 29 / 52 / 83 % above 10 m/s) over 4,051 tracks, 2,971 of them in the bins
claims.note: Each docs/02 table cell equals the JSON share (columns: object speed 0-0.2 / 0.2-0.4 / 0.4-0.8 / above 0.8 m/s). Drives A-C plus the first and last segment of 21 further drives.

claims.claim: Median |vRel - camera closing speed| (2 s box growth, 3-80 m, drives A-C) by age: 1.6 / 1.4 / 1.0 / 1.0 m/s for ages 11-25 / 26-50 / 51-80 / 81-125, and 0.6 m/s at the saturated age 126
claims.value: ages 11-25: 1.63, 26-50: 1.42, 51-80: 0.98, 81-125: 0.99, 126: 0.62 m/s (camera_pairs.parquet, figure filter vcam2 & 3-80 m, pooled over A-C)
claims.note: Camera pairs exist from age 11 upward.

claims.claim: Class 1 (new): 15 % of rows (median age 5), median 2-D speed 2.6 m/s
claims.note: 399-segment research run; share and speed over all occupied rows (age > 0, 2-D hypot of 64|10 / 74|10).

claims.claim: Class 2 (car): 75 % of rows, median 2-D speed 9.2 m/s, 1.8 m wide, 4.9 m long
claims.note: 399-segment research run (width and length over mature rows, age >= 60). On the bundled drives A-C the car share is 79.8 % with median 2-D speed 16.7 m/s, and the settled medians are 1.8 x 4.9 m (figure_numbers.json object_size).

claims.claim: Class 3 (large vehicle): 9 % of rows, median 2-D speed 4.9 m/s, 2.0 m wide, 5.7 m long
claims.note: 399-segment research run. On the bundled drives A-C the large-vehicle share is 8.2 %, median speed 16.9 m/s, width 2.0 m and length 6.1 m (figure_numbers.json object_size).

claims.claim: Class 4 (pedestrian): 1 % of rows, median 2-D speed 0.7 m/s, 0.5 m wide, 0.4 m long
claims.note: 399-segment research run. On the bundled drives A-C the pedestrian share is 0.2 % with mature width 0.5 m and length 0.4 m.

claims.claim: Class 6 (two-wheeler): rare, median 2-D speed 9.4 m/s, 0.7 m wide, 1.7 m long
claims.note: 399-segment research run, 90 mature rows.

claims.claim: Motion code 3: lateral velocity < -0.15 m/s on 393 / 393 mature samples
claims.value: 393/393 (137 confirmation + 192 discovery + 64 fresh, vy_negative = 1.0)
claims.note: Three partitions: 137 confirmation, 192 discovery, 64 fresh.

claims.claim: Motion code 4: lateral velocity > +0.15 m/s on 600 / 602 mature samples
claims.note: The 2 remaining samples are zero-band / sign boundary cases (SCR-158).

claims.claim: 131|4 equals the largest of the three lane weights or one less on 99.6-99.7 % of samples with a nonzero weight
claims.value: workspace 99.7 %; bundled 99.63 % (54,191 rows with a nonzero weight: 73.9 % = max, 25.7 % = max - 1)
claims.note: Scope: rows with at least one nonzero weight; rows with all three weights zero are 31.6 % of the bundled rows.

claims.claim: 136|4 restarts at 3-7 (median 4) when 112|3 becomes non-zero (1,279 onsets on the bundled drives) and climbs to 14-15
claims.value: bundled recompute (112|3 = bits 112-114, track-continuous onsets): 1,279 onsets, 136|4 at onset 3: 426, 4: 220, 5: 577, 6: 19, 7: 37; workspace: peak within 60 records on runs >= 20 records = 14 on 221 of 480, 15 on 132
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416, SCR-466; bundled slots.parquet
claims.note: 136|4 reads 15 on 91 % of rows with 112|3 = 0.

claims.claim: 112|3 by day has a range limit near 45 m in every ego-speed bin
claims.value: bundled day drives A and C: fraction non-zero 0.93-1.00 at 5-40 m, 0.06-0.52 at 45-50 m and 0.00 at 60-80 m, in each ego-speed bin (0-10 / 10-20 / 20-30 / 30-45 m/s)
claims.note: Drive B shows non-zero far-range rows rising at low ego speed (0.70 at 60-80 m, 0-10 m/s), the night / light-source mode.

claims.claim: Width agrees with the camera's vehicle width to about 0.05-0.07 m on 43 strict camera pairs (per-track median, candidate)
claims.value: mean absolute pair-median error 0.052 / 0.071 / 0.063 m over 9 / 17 / 17 strict pairs
claims.note: Provisional: both quantities use the native range.

claims.claim: 240|7 is higher when vRel disagrees with the camera: AUC 0.70 pooled, 0.62 within range, age and drive strata (30-60 m)
claims.value: AUC 0.70 at 30-60 m (per drive 0.65 / 0.73 / 0.67); 0.62 after stratifying by range, age and drive
claims.note: The stratified 0.62 is the figure with range and age held fixed. The 0.70 / 0.62 of SCR-466 (false closing against the ACC target at 60-80 m / 80-130 m) is a separate measurement.

claims.claim: 248|7 is sigma vy at about 0.37 m/s per count
claims.value: 0.3742-0.3775 m/s per count
claims.note: Owner's car (RAV4 2022); the second car scatters over 0.16-0.58 m/s per count (SIG-U1).

claims.claim: 200|7 is about 3.1 x 248|7 / speed on movers (interquartile 2.5-3.8)
claims.note: 700-segment corpus; fresh drives 2.65 / 3.31 / 4.14. The summary slot_camera_association.json carries the ratio.

claims.claim: 256|8 follows the frame scatter of ax most closely (Spearman 0.15; the other codes within +-0.06)
264|8 follows the frame scatter of ay (0.29) and of vy
claims.note: Fresh segments: 0.164 (ay), 0.091 (vy). 248|7 follows ay at 0.183 (fresh 0.165), so the ay link is shared by 248|7 and 264|8 on fresh drives.

claims.claim: 264|8 shrinks with age: median 11 at age 5-10, 4 at 40-60, 2 from age 60
claims.value: bundled median 264|8 (low 5 bits) = 11 at age 5-10; 4 at age 41-60; 2 at age 61-126 (pooled age >= 40: 2)
claims.note: The bundle holds the low 5 bits of the 8-bit field.

claims.claim: Saturated 64|10 = 1023 comes with 240|7 = 127 on all 35 bundled rows, in runs of 1-6 records on mature tracks at 34-97 m (9 events, 33 rows in the 700-segment corpus), and decays over a few records (drive B: 1023, 1016, 1004, 992, 981)
claims.value: workspace: 9 events, 33 mature rows, all age 126, 34-97 m, 240|7 = 127 throughout, runs of 1-6 records; bundled: 35 rows all with 240|7 = 127, 12 mature rows at 61-89 m, decay 1016, 1004, 992, 981 on B33
claims.note: The decay is one of four recovery modes. 23 young-track rows (age 1-20, 0-246 m) also read 1023; 34-97 m is the range of the mature rows.

claims.claim: State-2 score 16|8 steps by exactly 20 or 1 per cycle on every one of 6,330 mature state-2 updates (20 on 76 %, 1 on 24 %)
claims.value: 6,330 mature (age 60-126) updates, 0 exceptions: 20 x 4,845, 1 x 1,485; all state-2 edges of any age (18,804, same slot, age + 1): -20 x 17,791, -1 x 1,013
claims.note: Development / confirmation / further drives: 3,676 / 1,907 / 747 updates.

claims.claim: Bit 14 clears within the same allocation on 6,618 updates, 119 of them with both velocity codes unchanged
claims.value: 6,618 strict same-allocation clears; 119 = 33 + 49 + 9 + 5 + 23 with unchanged components
claims.source: research workspace SCR-293; bundled heading_default_state.json (the 119 by partition)
claims.note: The 6,618 is carried by this ledger.

claims.claim: The record CRC passes on 6,967 / 6,967 records of seven original logs
claims.value: 6967/6967, 0 failures, seven original rlogs
claims.note: Recompute on the 700-segment set: 677,754 / 677,754 CRC-valid records.

claims.claim: Counts are over 677,754 CRC-valid 0x85 records, 677,115 of which pair with their 0x80 record by counter and clock
claims.value: 677,754 CRC-valid 0x85 records; 677,115 pair with 0x80 (677,436 0x80 records)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: The prefix-copy counts (prefix_mask_700.json, 677,754 records) cover all CRC-valid records.

claims.claim: Byte 7 low 4 bits: counter, +1 per record on 99.997 % of steps; byte 15 bits 6-7: evenly spread 2-bit value that holds for 1-4 records
claims.value: byte 7 low nibble: uniform (each 6.25 %), +1 per record on 99.997 % of steps; byte 15 bits 6-7: each value 24-26 %, step 0 on 50.5 %, +1 on 11 %, +2 on 13 %, +3 (= -1) on 26 %, runs of 1-4 records
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Byte 7 high nibble is 2 (3 on 68 records).

claims.claim: Byte 16 low 5 bits: count-like quantity, 2-20 above a fixed 0x20; mean 3.5 at standstill, 10.4 at 14-22 m/s, 7.5 above 30 m/s; Spearman .58 with the number of populated cells, correlated with 0x80 header byte 13
claims.value: values 2-20 on 677,699 of 677,754 records (44 records 0-1, 11 with an upper part other than 0x20); means 3.50 (v < 0.1 m/s; 3.65 at v < 0.5) / 10.37 / 7.53; Spearman populated cells .575, speed .575, header byte 13 .387
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: The standstill mean follows the speed threshold (3.5 at v < 0.1 m/s).

claims.claim: Bytes 9, 11, 13 and 14 are zero in 99.1 % of records
claims.value: 99.12 % (5,980 nonzero records in 374 segments of 677,754)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: 5,980 nonzero records in 374 segments of 677,754.

claims.claim: 79|1 is the same in cells 2 and 3 on 99 % of rows; set on 79-80 % of cells 2 / 3 and 43-44 % of cells 8 / 9, rarely elsewhere
claims.value: set on 79.4 / 80.4 % of populated cells 2 / 3 and 43.7 / 42.8 % of cells 8 / 9; cells 2 and 3 equal on 98.98 % of rows with both populated (4,082 mismatches in 285 segments of 399,473; 92.5 % over all rows); public lane_cells.parquet: 98.7 % of 10,301 rows; cell 4 set on 21 rows (0.02 %); cells 0, 1, 5-7: 0 set rows

claims.claim: Cells 8 / 9 correlate with cells 2 / 3 in offset at 0.98 / 0.99
claims.value: Spearman 0.982 (2,8), 0.989 (3,9) over 392k/391k rows (Pearson 0.94/0.97); public lane_cells.parquet Spearman 0.994/0.997
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Spearman; Pearson on the full corpus is 0.94 / 0.97.

claims.claim: Cells 8 and 9 share 24|4, 28|1 and 44|4 on every row and 20|4 on every row where both are populated
claims.value: 24|4, 28|1, 44|4 equal on all 677,754 rows; 20|4 equal on 100 % of rows where both are populated (85 % of all rows); cells 2 / 3 agree on 23 / 46 / 64 / 65 % of rows for the four fields in the same order
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Scope of the 20|4 statement: rows where both cells are populated.

claims.claim: Camera-quality-like fields (24|4 low bits = 1 and bit 27 set, 20|4 ~ 5, 28|1 = 0, 44|4 = 2) go with a camera lane probability >= 0.99
claims.note: Tendencies measured on the research corpus (71 %, 81-100 %).

claims.claim: Cells 6 and 7 take either side (|offset| 1-8 m) and follow the camera's left outer line 61-76 % of the time
claims.value: SCR-416: both signs, |offset| 1-8 m, camera left-outer line 61 / 76 %; against openpilot's road-edge estimate: route-centred r .92-.94, route- and side-centred r .36-.46, median error .45-.61 m, p90 1.3-3.0 m
claims.note: Cells 6 and 7 track openpilot's road edge to a median 0.5-0.6 m and stay unnamed.

claims.claim: 0|9 falls about 4.1-4.4 codes per metre driven in monotone runs of cells 8 and 9
claims.value: source 4.1-4.4 (r .90 / .82, 4.5k / 5.4k runs); recompute (non-increasing runs >= 10 records, drop >= 5, v > 1 m/s): pooled drop / distance 4.17 (cell 8) / 4.09 (cell 9), r .92 / .88; per-run median slope 4.66 / 4.70
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: The run definition moves the number by about 10 %; cells 2 / 3 fall about 2.2-2.4 codes per metre (r .23-.28).

claims.claim: 80|6 is confidence-like (0-50); cell 1 holds 0, 15 or 50 on every row; cell 4 holds the same three values on 99.98 % of populated rows
claims.value: range 0-50 (cells 8 / 9: 0-48); cell 1: 0 / 15 / 50 on every row; cell 4: 0 / 15 / 50 on 99.98 % of populated rows (22 rows hold 34, 39, 43 and similar); cells 0 and 5 constant 50, cells 6 / 7 constant 0
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures

claims.claim: The 15 bits 64|15 correlate with the gyro curvature (yaw rate / speed) at rho 0.70; the whole 16-bit word at 0.44
claims.value: SCR-416: -0.70 (low 15 bits) vs -0.45 (whole word) against device-z / speed; recompute (livePose angularVelocityDevice_z +-0.5 s mean, -z / v, v > 5 m/s): cell 2 0.700 vs 0.442, cell 3 0.686 vs 0.438, cells 2 + 3 pooled 0.693 vs 0.440, cells 8 / 9 0.65 / 0.64 vs 0.31 / 0.32
claims.source: research workspace SCR-416; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Cells 2 / 3; the sign is positive against left-positive yaw.

claims.claim: 0x23B width: cars read about 175 cm inside 30 m and 165 cm at 90 m (class 1)
claims.source: research workspace SCR-466; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Range-band medians are in the value field; acc_target_frames.json holds the class medians.

claims.claim: 0x239 object-list flag is set on 99 % of frames when an object-list track sits at the target's position
claims.source: research workspace SCR-466; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: acc_target_frames.json carries the by-list-size shares (0.88-0.95 with a matching track).

claims.claim: 0x191 score 1|7: 91-100 while a target is active, 127 = idle sentinel
claims.note: Active values: 100 on 454,786, 99 on 82,243, 91 on 2,929 of 608,186 active frames; the DBC comment carries the definition.

claims.claim: Counter 43|5 grows with target age: about 20 at age 10-20, saturating at 30
claims.source: research workspace SCR-466; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Two independent recomputes agree on median 20; saturation at 30 from age 45-50.

claims.claim: The object list's class for a class-2 ACC target is large vehicle on 92 % of 20,394 matched frames
claims.note: For the 0x191 / 0x192 truck-template summary (22:23:120) the share is 81 % over 4,957 frames.

claims.claim: 0x192 lateral (code - 2048) x 0.015 m: median residual 0.01 m
claims.note: Residual MAD 0.005 m (0x192) / 0.012 m (0x194), fitted at the 1/64 m unit (unit change moves it by about 4 %).

claims.claim: The speed from a 1 s slope of the 0x192 range matches the ACC speed for the same car: correlation 0.98, median difference 0.18 m/s
claims.source: bundled summary_tracks.json (current_units_recompute); research workspace SCR-463, SCR-478
claims.note: Current units (ACC speed 0.125 m/s per code, summary range (code - 160) / 16 m). The 1 s slope MAE / RMSE come from SCR-478 over 700 segments.

claims.claim: During object-list velocity excursions the summary speed stays with the ACC speed in 490 of 490 cycles (0x192) and 98 of 98 (0x194)
claims.note: Excursion = native - ACC speed < -2.5 m/s at the current ACC unit.

claims.claim: Optical check: false closings > 2.5 m/s at 60-80 m fall from 14.9 % (object list) to about 10 % (summary); the summary is closer in 97 % of object-list false closings
claims.source: bundled summary_tracks.json (current_units_recompute, optical_check); research workspace SCR-429
claims.note: Current-unit values are approximate (window-to-summary matching at the earlier range scale). The summary leads from 40 to 80 m; beyond 80 m the median errors are 0.98 (object list) and 1.02 m/s (summary).

claims.claim: Summaries are present while the ACC target is idle at a median 60 m (0x194: 79 m); about half lie beyond 60 m (0x194: 65 %)
claims.source: bundled summary_tracks.json (current_units_recompute, present_without_acc_target); research workspace SCR-426
claims.note: Range-scale dependent: the values are at the current summary range scale.

claims.claim: 0x190 cycle counter: +3 per cycle on 99.996 % of cycles
0x240 / 0x244 carry light-source records at night: 71 of 698 one-minute segments, 35 of 114 on a second set, ramping in over three minutes at dusk
claims.note: Counts from the SCR-466 context census; context_24x.json carries the frame layout (two records per frame: type nibble, 3 flag bits, 13-bit signed value, 8-bit value).

claims.claim: 0x680 stationary roadside object typically 8 m to the side
claims.source: research workspace SCR-462; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Median |y| 8.0 m (IQR 4.76-11.56 m, n = 43,561) at the 0.015 m lateral unit; computed from the research captures.

claims.claim: 0x23B CRC-8 passes on 3,615 of 3,616 distinct payloads over 2.05 M frames, and on 30,056 of 30,058 frames of fresh drives (the exceptions are the startup frame 00 0f ff)
claims.note: Fresh-drive counts from the research workspace SCR-416 result.

claims.claim: Tracker byte A: 35-36 on a steady target, 44-50 while the target accelerates harder than 1.2 m/s2, median 48-74 while it brakes; byte B: about 86 for a stopped target, 128-135 for a steady mover, toward 240 within half a second of a maneuver; 78-88 % explained by the target's kinematics
claims.note: The 44-50 range for accelerating targets is the research-run figure; the bundled bin medians read 47.

claims.claim: yRel side is correct on 97.9-99.3 % of off-centre targets against the camera
Closing rate over relative speed gives 15.93 / 16.01 codes per metre on two calibration routes
claims.note: The velocity side is 0xB4 ego speed, which reads 1-1.5 % below GPS.

claims.claim: Camera ground contact minus radar: -0.01 m (A), +0.22 m (C), +0.72 m (B, hilly), the size of a 0.19 degree camera-pitch error at B's median 17.5 m
claims.source: research workspace SCR-090; bundled ground_contact.parquet (5-25 m, RADAR_TO_CAMERA 1.52 m)
claims.note: Pitch error that reproduces B's offset: 0.19 degrees at 17.5 m, 0.25 degrees at 15 m.

claims.claim: Ego-lane objects stay within 0.1-0.3 m of the lane centre from 15 to 130 m on straight road (two calibration routes)
claims.note: Fitted at the 1/64 m scale (a factor 0.96 at 0.015 m, small). Exploratory ego-lane medians on the bundled slots.parquet (all road geometry, per drive) span -0.47 to +0.29 m.

claims.claim: Toyota 0xB4 reads about 1-1.5 % below GPS and wheel speed
claims.note: Bundled data: 0.9-1.5 % below GPS (A 1.5, B 0.9, C 1.2) and 1.3-1.4 % below carState wheel speed.

claims.claim: Stopped targets 5-30 m: vRel RMS 0.54 m/s on settled tracks (B and C)
claims.note: All-age RMS 0.71 (B) / 0.55 (C); the doc links review_followup.json.

claims.claim: On decelerating leads the radar's speed leads the camera's by 0.2-0.4 s
claims.note: Measured on the owner's StarPilot closed-loop drives (radar vLead against openpilot's camera lead).

claims.claim: Settled-track range jumps by about 3 % of range from record to record, decorrelating within about 5 cycles
claims.note: Increments of range minus integrated vRel rise to about 5 cycles (2.4 % to 6.2 % of range at 40-80 m) and then slowly with vRel drift.

claims.claim: A real closing: the radar lead reads 24.7 m against the vision model's 36.8 m while the camera box grows 27 % over the 2 s shown
claims.note: Over the 1.5 s window of the radar's closing the box grows 16.5 %; the 2 s between the two shot frames give 27 %.

claims.claim: Idle payload table: rates, DLC and idle payloads of the nine car-bus messages
claims.source: research workspace SCR-459, SCR-481; bundled radar_car_bus_messages.json
claims.note: 0x494 / 0x4FF rates and the 0x343 33 Hz rate come from the SCR-481 census; 0x366 idle on owner drive O2 reads 50.. (2,097 frames) or 52.. (592).

claims.claim: 0x411 reads 40 20 ... (PCS_INDICATOR 1) from about 0.2 s to 3 s after each of 27 cold starts
claims.source: research workspace SCR-459; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: The 27 start-up segments are part of the 752 owner segments that carry 0x411; 40 20 lasts about 3 frames at 1 Hz.

claims.claim: Eight 0x366 reports carry codes 442-506; five same-tail steps among them close at 20-28 m/s by their distances; code - 512 fits (mean difference 2.9 m/s)
claims.note: Codes below 256 are the domain the ACC target confirms.

claims.claim: 0x366 byte 0 is 0x50 or 0x52; byte 4 bits 3-7 vary (flags); the low three bits of byte 5 are constant; it arrives about 90 ms after 0x365
claims.source: research workspace SCR-466, SCR-481; recomputed from the research captures
claims.note: Bit numbering is LSB within the byte (byte 4 = (b >> 3) varies); 0x52 occurs on owner drive O2.

claims.claim: Message rates 0x24D 1 Hz, 0x24F 33 Hz, 0x210 5 Hz
claims.source: recomputed from one full owner road drive (bus-1 frames, per one-minute segment median)
claims.note: Per one-minute segment medians over 39 segments of one owner drive: 0x24F 33.32-33.36 Hz, 0x210 4.98-5.0 Hz.
